relation_statement: Every trainable submodule's weight-gradient computation must be invoked exactly once per backward pass under fine-grained backward_dw scheduling with latent MoE projections enabled.
observable_signal: Per-parameter main_grad norm of the latent projection weights: exactly zero across all microbatches/steps (and parameter values frozen at init) witnesses the missing gradient computation.
validity_precondition: MoE layer with moe_latent_size set and separate backward_dw scheduling for routed/shared experts
evidence_from_issue: Latent MoE backward_dw never calls fc1_latent_proj/fc2_latent_proj.backward_dw, so gradient for the latent projection weights is silently zero
evidence_from_fix: MoELayer.backward_dw only invoked self.experts.backward_dw() ... latent projection layers were never asked to compute their weight gradients, so their main_grad stayed at zero; the optimizer applied (lr * 0) every step

relation_statement: Per-module low-precision scaling state (amax history / DelayedScaling recipe) must evolve identically whether the layer runs eagerly or via CUDA-graph replay, under FP4 training with graph capture enabled.
observable_signal: Per-module amax/scale values compared between graph replay and an eager reference step; monotone drift of FP4 scale away from target across replays witnesses the skipped recipe restoration.
validity_precondition: FP4 (NVFP4) DelayedScaling training with CUDA graphs enabled and FP8 inactive
evidence_from_issue: treats fp4_enabled as fp8 only, skipping the per-module FP-recipe restoration on FP4 paths so saved scaling factors drift each replay
evidence_from_fix: With FP4 active but FP8 inactive, the recipe restore branch was skipped, so each replay used a stale amax history ... every step shifted the FP4 scale away from the target

relation_statement: Layers explicitly pinned to bf16 must execute their GEMMs in bf16 (never be cast into FP8/FP4 paths) even when global low-precision training and CUDA-graph capture are enabled.
observable_signal: Compute dtype / quantization wrapping of the captured attention-linear GEMMs: FP8 cast applied to a keep-in-bf16 module witnesses the violation.
validity_precondition: Mamba/hybrid model with keep-mamba-stack-attention-linear-in-bf16 and config.fp8 or config.fp4 enabled with CUDA graph capture
evidence_from_issue: enables FP8 capture for keep-mamba-stack-attention-linear-in-bf16 layers, casting frozen-bf16 attention linears into FP8 inside the captured graph
evidence_from_fix: set self.fp8_enabled unconditionally ... capturing those layers with FP8 enabled wrapped their GEMMs in FP8 cast paths, silently quantizing weights that were intentionally meant to stay in bf16

relation_statement: The quantization scale/amax state used by the recomputed forward must be consistent with the original forward pass under FP4 training with activation recompute enabled.
observable_signal: Amax-history length/content and per-module scale compared between the original forward and the recomputed forward; a recompute pass that does not extend amax history witnesses the violation.
validity_precondition: MoE layer with moe_layer_recompute enabled, config.fp4 set and config.fp8 unset
evidence_from_issue: FP4 recompute uses tensor_parallel.checkpoint and loses FP4 amax tracking
evidence_from_fix: te_checkpoint selected only when self.config.fp8 ... amax history is not extended for the recomputed forward, yielding mismatched scales between forward and recompute

relation_statement: The number of experts selected per token by group-limited routing must equal the configured top-k under grouped MoE routing.
observable_signal: Per-token count of selected experts (and per-group selection counts) compared to the configured topk; selecting num_groups instead of topk witnesses the violation.
validity_precondition: MoE router using group_limited_topk (grouped/device-limited routing)
evidence_from_issue: group_limited_topk uses num_groups instead of topk in inner topk
evidence_from_fix: (no root_cause text provided; inferred from title: wrong k passed to the inner topk call)

relation_statement: Each context-parallel rank's rotary embedding slice must cover exactly the token positions of its own sequence partition, so forward activations are invariant to the CP degree.
observable_signal: Per-CP-rank rotary position index range compared against the rank's sequence-partition offsets (or activations vs a CP=1 reference); slicing the wrong axis / wrong cp_group witnesses the mismatch.
validity_precondition: Multimodal rotary embedding (mrope) with context_parallel_world_size > 1 and sequence dimension at index 0 post-transpose
evidence_from_issue: slices rotary embedding along the wrong dimension and omits cp_group when CP is enabled, so each CP rank sees the wrong rotary position embedding
evidence_from_fix: get_pos_emb_on_this_cp_rank was called with seq_dim=1 and no cp_group ... each CP rank ended up with a rotary slice that does not correspond to its own sequence partition

relation_statement: The activation tensor received by the next pipeline stage must equal the tensor produced by the sending stage under PP>1 with asynchronous isend/irecv.
observable_signal: Checksum of the sent activation buffer at isend time vs the received tensor on the next stage; corruption from buffer reuse before isend completion witnesses the violation.
validity_precondition: Hybrid Mamba model with virtual pipeline parallelism, post_process and post_layer_norm both True, inter-stage tensor sent via isend/irecv
evidence_from_issue: assigns make_viewless_tensor result to local 'output' but returns 'hidden_states', sending a non-viewless aliased tensor between hybrid VPP stages
evidence_from_fix: the make_viewless_tensor call had no effect ... the underlying buffer was reused before isend completed, and the next stage received corrupted activations

relation_statement: Parameter storage dtype must match the configured mixed-precision dtype (bf16 config must materialize bf16 params) under the DSL config path, just as the legacy CLI path guarantees.
observable_signal: Dtype of materialized model parameters at init compared to mixed_precision_dtype (fp32 params under bf16 config witness the violation), plus roughly doubled parameter memory footprint.
validity_precondition: Hybrid model built via the Python DSL recipe API with mixed_precision_dtype='bf16' and params_dtype left at default
evidence_from_issue: does not derive params_dtype from mixed_precision_dtype, so models with mixed_precision_dtype='bf16' silently keep params_dtype=fp32
evidence_from_fix: produced a TransformerConfig with bf16=True but params_dtype=torch.float32 ... parameters materialized in fp32 and cast on every forward, doubling memory and changing numerics relative to the legacy path

relation_statement: Every sub-optimizer's parameters and optimizer state must be restored from the checkpoint after resume, matching the saved values, under a chained optimizer with a single model chunk.
observable_signal: Post-resume checksum of expert parameters / sub-optimizer states vs checkpoint contents; expert parameters equal to fresh default initialization after resume witnesses the skipped load.
validity_precondition: ChainedOptimizer with multiple sub-optimizers (e.g. dense + MoE) and a single global model chunk, loading via split_state_dict
evidence_from_issue: only assigns to state_dicts[0], leaving all other sub-optimizers unaware of the model state and silently skipping their load
evidence_from_fix: state_dicts[1:] left as None ... sub-optimizers beyond index 0 silently skipped loading; the model proceeded with default-initialized expert parameters after a checkpoint resume

relation_statement: The set of gradients gathered for the global norm must match the set of trainable parameters with gradients (no parameter silently contributing nothing) under FP8 + precision-aware optimizer settings.
observable_signal: Reported grad_norm value: exactly 0.0 while the loss is changing (empty grads_for_norm set) witnesses the violation; also count of tensors contributing to the norm vs trainable-parameter count.
validity_precondition: use_precision_aware_optimizer enabled with FP8 non-delayed/DS scaling, gradient clipping or count_zeros active
evidence_from_issue: FP8 + precision-aware paths read param.decoupled_grad which is None and report grad_norm=0
evidence_from_fix: the buggy gate took the precision-aware path anyway, attempting to read param.decoupled_grad (None), so grads_for_norm came back empty and grad_norm computed to 0.0; without proper clipping the optimizer could overshoot

relation_statement: The logged z-loss metric must be averaged over the participating ranks so the reported value equals the cross-rank mean (identical on all ranks) under multi-rank training.
observable_signal: Per-rank logged z-loss values: divergence across ranks (no reduction applied) witnesses the missing avg_group.
validity_precondition: z-loss enabled and metric tracking/logging active across multiple ranks
evidence_from_issue: z-loss metric tracking missing avg_group — not averaged across ranks
evidence_from_fix: (no root_cause text provided; inferred from title: reduction group not passed to the metric averaging)

relation_statement: The reported aux_loss must carry the correct normalization (not be scaled by the TP world size, and be reduced over the intended group) under TP>1.
observable_signal: Logged aux_loss magnitude vs the true per-token auxiliary loss: an offset by exactly the TP world-size factor witnesses the wrong scaling.
validity_precondition: MoE aux_loss metric logging with tensor parallelism enabled
evidence_from_issue: aux_loss metric incorrectly scaled by TP world_size, missing reduce_group
evidence_from_fix: (no root_cause text provided; inferred from title: scaling by TP world size applied without the corresponding reduce_group)

relation_statement: Tied word-embedding replicas on different pipeline stages must remain identical after every optimizer step (hence must be routed to the same optimizer) under PP>=2 with tied embeddings.
observable_signal: Checksum/norm of the tied word_embeddings replica on PP rank 0 vs the MTP-only last stage after each optimizer step; divergence witnesses the split AdamW-vs-Muon routing.
validity_precondition: Muon optimizer enabled, MTP-only final PP stage owning a tied word_embeddings replica, share-embeddings-and-output-weights active
evidence_from_issue: tied word_embeddings on MTP-only last PP stage routed to Muon instead of Adam
evidence_from_fix: is_embedding_or_output_parameter only set when pre_process is True ... the two tied copies receive different optimizer updates (AdamW vs Muon Newton-Schulz), causing silent divergence

relation_statement: Each step's observed gradient norm must be incorporated exactly once into the grad-norm EMA update (the EMA must not be updated from itself) whenever adaptive clipping is active.
observable_signal: grad_norm_exp_avg trajectory vs an EMA recomputed from the logged per-step grad norms; an EMA that never responds to grad-norm changes witnesses the self-referential update.
validity_precondition: Adaptive gradient clipping with grad_norm_exp_avg tracking enabled
evidence_from_issue: grad_norm_exp_avg EMA self-referential update — adaptive clipping broken
evidence_from_fix: (no root_cause text provided; inferred from title: EMA updated from its own previous value instead of the new grad-norm observation)

relation_statement: Attention outputs must remain finite (masked bias values must be representable in the compute dtype, e.g. finfo.min instead of -inf) under autocast mixed precision with padded/masked sequences.
observable_signal: NaN count in attention outputs / loss once masked tokens are present; presence of -inf bias entries in a bf16/fp16 SDP call witnesses the unsafe downcast.
validity_precondition: AMP/autocast (bf16 or fp16) with padded sequences requiring attention masking via scaled_dot_product_attention
evidence_from_issue: SDP attention bias not cast to autocast dtype, -inf downcasts to NaNs in mixed precision
evidence_from_fix: bias created in fp32 with -inf ... downcasting -inf propagates through softmax and produces NaNs; fix uses torch.finfo(target_dtype).min and casts the bias before the SDP call

relation_statement: Reported cumulative Gflops must be proportional to the total number of tokens processed (accumulating monotonically across resumes) whenever speed monitoring is enabled.
observable_signal: Ratio of reported cumulative Gflops to global_total_tokens; a per-step reset or a value scaling with batch count instead of token count witnesses the violation.
validity_precondition: Speed/FLOPs monitoring enabled, especially across checkpoint restarts
evidence_from_issue: FLOPs counter multiplies per-sequence flops by global batch size every step instead of accumulating per token
evidence_from_fix: after resume the running total was overwritten/reset per step rather than treated as cumulative; fix assigns Gflops = (fwd+bck) * global_total_tokens / 1e9

relation_statement: The reduced gradient norm must count each gradient exactly once (reduction over the shard group, not WORLD) so the reported norm does not scale with the number of HSDP replicas.
observable_signal: Reported global grad norm vs the norm computed within a single replica's shard group; inflation by the replica count witnesses the wrong process group.
validity_precondition: FSDP HYBRID_SHARD/HYBRID_SHARD_ZERO2 with more than one model replica and gradient clipping or grad-norm metrics enabled
evidence_from_issue: clip_grads_and_collect_metrics reduces grad norm over the global PG instead of the HSDP shard PG
evidence_from_fix: each replica holds a full copy of the gradients, so reducing over WORLD double-counts grads across replicas; fix routes every reduce/all_reduce through an explicit process_group

relation_statement: An optimizer step and an outlier flag must be mutually exclusive: the optimizer must step exactly when the loss/grad-norm is NOT flagged as an outlier, whenever outlier skipping is enabled.
observable_signal: Optimizer step count vs batch count and the per-step is_outlier flag: parameters unchanged on normal batches (and updated only on outlier batches) witnesses the inverted gate.
validity_precondition: ce_loss_outlier_detector or grad_norm_outlier_detector enabled
evidence_from_issue: Outlier-loss skip-step logic inverted: optimizer steps only when loss IS an outlier
evidence_from_fix: should_step was AND-ed with is_outlier, meaning the optimizer only stepped on outlier steps and silently skipped normal training steps; fix negates is_outlier

relation_statement: The runtime device placement and distributed mode must match the actually available/requested backend (CUDA hosts must not be silently rewritten to MPS/CPU with distributed disabled) at startup.
observable_signal: Device type of initialized model parameters and the active distributed world size vs the launched configuration; CUDA available but init_device forced to 'mps' with distributed off witnesses the violation.
validity_precondition: Training entrypoint performing backend/device auto-detection
evidence_from_issue: torch.device('mps') used as boolean check is always truthy, forces every run into MPS/CPU mode
evidence_from_fix: the condition is always True because torch.device(...) returns a non-None object ... unconditionally rewrites init_device to 'mps' and disables distributed training even on CUDA hosts; fix uses torch.backends.mps.is_available()

relation_statement: Parameters loaded from a checkpoint must equal the saved values (loading must be idempotent, applying no additional muP rescaling) when resuming a muP model.
observable_signal: Post-load parameter checksums/norms vs checkpoint contents; weights uniformly shrunk/grown by the muP width factor after from_checkpoint witnesses the double rescale.
validity_precondition: model.use_mup=true and OLMo.from_checkpoint() used to resume
evidence_from_issue: muP set_base_shapes rescales parameters again when loading from a checkpoint, doubling the muP scaling
evidence_from_fix: parameters are already in muP-scaled space, so the rescale fires a second time and silently shrinks/grows weights by the muP factor; fix adds mup_rescale_params=False from from_checkpoint

relation_statement: Per-parameter-group lr/weight_decay must retain their muP-scaled values after checkpoint restore (not be reset to the single base value for every group) when resuming a muP run.
observable_signal: Post-restore lr ratio between matrix-like and other param groups: all groups equal to cfg base lr (muP width scaling wiped) witnesses the violation.
validity_precondition: muP enabled (MuAdamW) with per-group width multipliers, training resumed from checkpoint
evidence_from_issue: Restart LR/weight-decay reset uses cfg.learning_rate for every param group, ignoring per-group muP scaling
evidence_from_fix: reset every group's lr/initial_lr/weight_decay to the base values, wiping muP scaling; fix tags each muP group with mup_lr/mup_weight_decay and uses those when resetting

relation_statement: Attention must respect causal ordering: token t may attend only to positions <= t (future positions masked) in autoregressive training.
observable_signal: Attention probability mass on future positions (must be zero); equivalently, perturbing a future token must not change the output at earlier positions.
validity_precondition: Causal (autoregressive) attention layers during training
evidence_from_issue: Attention causal mask inverted — future tokens attend to past
evidence_from_fix: 1 - triu() masks the lower triangle instead of upper, inverting causal attention

relation_statement: The readout (output projection) weights must be initialized to zero, per the muP prescription, when use_mup is enabled.
observable_signal: Norm of ff_out weights immediately after reset_parameters: any nonzero value under muP witnesses the overwrite by init_normal.
validity_precondition: model.use_mup=true; reset_parameters invoked from __init__
evidence_from_issue: ff_out readout reset overwrites muP zero-init weights with normal-distribution values
evidence_from_fix: reset_parameters always called init_normal on ff_out, including under muP where ff_out must be initialized to zero; breaks the muP coordinate-check property; fix skips init_normal when use_mup

relation_statement: The muP attention scale must equal sqrt(base_d)/d, matching the standard-parameterization scale 1/sqrt(d) exactly at the base width, whenever use_mup is enabled on the SDP path.
observable_signal: The numeric attention scale factor applied in SDP vs the prescribed sqrt(mup_base_n_heads)/head_dim; a 1/d scale at base width witnesses the mismatch.
validity_precondition: model.use_mup=true on the scaled-dot-product attention path (not flash varlen)
evidence_from_issue: muP attention scale uses 1/d instead of sqrt(base_d)/d, mismatching the SP scale at the base width
evidence_from_fix: the scale differs from 1/sqrt(d) even at the base width, silently changing attention temperature; fix uses sqrt(mup_base_n_heads)/q.size(-1) so the scale matches SP at base width

relation_statement: Under Post-LN (norm_after), the attention normalization must be applied to the attention output immediately before the residual add — not to the QKV projection output — in every transformer block.
observable_signal: Statistics (variance/RMS) of the tensor added to the residual stream: an unnormalized attention output entering the residual add under norm_after witnesses the misplaced norm.
validity_precondition: model.norm_after=true in the sequential transformer block forward
evidence_from_issue: norm_after path applies attn_norm to (att_proj output) instead of to the attention output, leaving residual unnormed
evidence_from_fix: attn_norm was applied to the QKV projection output before attention; Post-LN requires applying attn_norm to the attention output before the residual add — silently changes model semantics

relation_statement: After a weights-only restore (restore_dataloader=False), the training step counter must be reset to 0 consistently with the other run counters so the LR schedule starts from warmup.
observable_signal: global_step and the LR value at the first resumed step: step equal to the checkpoint's step (e.g. 50000) with warmup skipped witnesses the missing reset.
validity_precondition: Resume from checkpoint with cfg.restore_dataloader=False (fresh run from saved weights)
evidence_from_issue: global_step not reset when restore_dataloader=False, so resumed runs keep the checkpoint's step counter
evidence_from_fix: restore_checkpoint() resets epoch and token counters but forgot to reset global_step; the LR scheduler starts at the checkpoint's step, silently skipping warmup and using a much smaller LR

relation_statement: Each epoch must consume every training example exactly once (the dataset start offset must reset to 0 at each epoch boundary) in multi-epoch training.
observable_signal: Per-epoch consumed-sample count vs dataset length, or dataset.start_index at epoch start (must be 0); skipping the first N instances of the new epoch witnesses the violation.
validity_precondition: max_epochs > 1 and an epoch boundary reached during training
evidence_from_issue: Multi-epoch training does not reset dataset.start_index, so the next epoch resumes from the previous epoch's offset
evidence_from_fix: on epoch rollover Trainer reset epoch counters and reshuffled but never reset dataset.start_index; the IterableDataset skipped the first global_train_examples_seen_this_epoch instances, silently dropping them

relation_statement: All-reduced gradient norms must be normalized by the number of model replicas so the reported norm equals the true single-replica value under HSDP.
observable_signal: Reported grad_norm vs the norm computed inside one replica: inflation by exactly the replica count N witnesses the hardcoded num_model_replicas=1.
validity_precondition: FSDP HYBRID_SHARD with num_model_replicas > 1 and metric collection enabled
evidence_from_issue: Optimizer collects metrics with num_model_replicas == 1 hardcoded, so HSDP norms are N times too large
evidence_from_fix: each replica contributed identical gradient norms; without dividing by the replica count, all_reduce sums them and the reported norm is N times the true value, leading to spurious clipping decisions

relation_statement: All-reduced parameter/gradient sums and norms must be divided by the number of model replicas before use, so logged optimizer metrics equal the true per-replica values under HSDP.
observable_signal: Logged per-param avg and grad_norm metrics vs values computed within a single replica: inflation by the replica count N witnesses the missing division.
validity_precondition: HSDP with num_model_replicas > 1, collect_param_metrics=True, param-norm metrics logged
evidence_from_issue: Reduced sums/norms not divided by num_model_replicas in HSDP, optimizer metrics inflated by replica count
evidence_from_fix: after dist.all_reduce(SUM), identical replica contributions are summed N times; fix divides the all-reduced tensors by self.num_model_replicas before splitting and using

relation_statement: Normalization-layer parameters must be assigned exclusively to the no-decay group (never receive weight decay) when no_decay_norm_and_bias is enabled.
observable_signal: Effective weight_decay hyperparameter attached to each norm parameter's group: a nonzero decay on q_norm/k_norm/ff_norm weights witnesses the misrouting.
validity_precondition: no_decay_norm_and_bias enabled and the model has norm parameters whose FQN ends at .norm.weight-style leaves (e.g. q_norm.weight)
evidence_from_issue: param-group classifier uses '.norm.' regex requiring trailing dot, treating q_norm/k_norm/ff_norm leaf weights as decay params
evidence_from_fix: the substring '.norm.' only matches when there is a child name after .norm ... the weight is silently routed to the decay group, applying weight_decay to a normalization layer's gain

relation_statement: Cached rotary sin/cos tensors must be cast to match the query/key compute dtype before use under mixed-precision training.
observable_signal: Dtype of pos_sin/pos_cos at the point of application vs q/k dtype (fp32 cache meeting bf16/fp16 activations witnesses the mismatch).
validity_precondition: Mixed-precision (bf16/fp16) training with rotary position embeddings using a cached sin/cos table
evidence_from_issue: RoPE sin/cos missing type_as — dtype mismatch in mixed precision
evidence_from_fix: pos_sin/pos_cos cached in float32, not cast to match q_ dtype (bf16/fp16)
